study_title: Providing Public Workforce Services to Job Seekers: 30-Month Impact Findings on the WIA Adult and Dislocated Worker Programs
program: Workforce Investment Act Adult and Dislocated Worker programs

assignment_groups.full_wia: Access to core, intensive, and training services.
assignment_groups.core_and_intensive: Access to core and intensive services; restricted from WIA-funded training for the first 15 months.
assignment_groups.core_only: Access to core services; restricted from WIA-funded intensive and training services for the first 15 months.

study_design.estimand_note: Intent-to-treat contrasts between randomized access groups; the training contrast is full WIA versus core-and-intensive, and the intensive-services contrast is core-and-intensive versus core-only.

cumulative_earnings_2012_usd.interpretation: The randomized contrasts identify the effect of access to the specified historical WIA service tier under the study design. The survey and NDNH measures use different follow-up windows and must not be pooled.

service_receipt_percent.interpretation: Crossover and access to non-WIA services narrowed treatment-control differences. The nine-percentage-point training take-up contrast makes the training-service impact evidence inconclusive.

credential_and_completion_percent.denominator_note: Publisher-reported group percentages retain the report's outcome definitions and analysis universes; they are not counts or current WIOA performance indicators.

benefit_cost_analysis_per_customer_2012_.interpretation: Historical study benefit-cost estimates per customer, not budget savings, recoveries, or present-day fiscal scores. Customer gains and taxpayer gains are distinct components of the social perspective.

limitations: The experiment evaluated WIA, the predecessor to WIOA, using applicants enrolled from November 2011 through April 2013 in 28 participating local areas.
The randomized offer changed access to WIA-funded service tiers, not receipt of all employment or training services; crossover and community alternatives reduced service-use contrasts.
Restrictions on the core-and-intensive and core-only groups lasted only the first 15 months, while outcomes extend to 30 or 36 months.
Veterans and other study exclusions limit the population to which the impact estimates directly apply.
The survey and NDNH earnings series use different sources, samples, and follow-up windows.
Benefit-cost estimates are in 2012 dollars per historical WIA customer and cannot be attached to FY2025 OMB subfunction 504 outlays.
prohibited_inferences: Do not treat the nonsignificant negative training contrasts as proof that training harms earnings.
Do not transport the historical WIA impacts mechanically to current WIOA participants, service designs, labor markets, or funding levels.
Do not label benefit-cost values as fraud, waste, recoverable savings, budget authority, obligations, or actual outlays.
Do not divide current Training and Employment subfunction spending by these study impacts or customer benefits.
